subdomain: 2.1 Select appropriate Claude models based on trade-offs

en.question: A service extracts delivery dates from short messages. On representative messages and difficult date formats, both candidate models meet the required accuracy and response-time thresholds. Model A has stronger general benchmark results; Model B has lower measured operating cost for this service, including retries. Which model-selection decision is best supported?

options.text: Choose Model A because its general benchmark advantage outweighs the service-specific results.
options.note: A broader benchmark does not establish additional value for this extraction contract. Both candidates already meet the stated task and timing requirements.

options.text: Choose Model B and continue monitoring the extraction and latency thresholds.
options.note: Use-case measurements support the lower-cost candidate when it satisfies the required capability and speed. Continued monitoring can detect changes in input mix or failure rates.

options.text: Alternate between the models to improve average capability without changing the evaluation.
options.note: Alternation introduces a mixed operating policy without evidence that it improves this task. Its combined quality and cost would need evaluation before adoption.

options.text: Choose Model A and shorten the prompt until its token cost matches Model B.
options.note: Shortening the prompt can remove necessary instructions and changes the evaluated configuration. Matching input spend alone does not establish equivalent operating cost or quality.
